texts.before: The Alpen-Adria-Galerie announces an exhibition of works by Drago Druškovič for the turn of the year 2026/27. Opening on 15 December 2026 at 18:00; on view until 31 January 2027. Title and further details have not been published yet; the gallery reserves the right to make changes. Source: stadtgalerie.net

Classes from 17 primary schools across Carinthia showed what they had made in the kidsmobil workshop “Kleine Künstler*innen für eine große Vielfalt” of the wissens.wert.welt at the kärnten.museum: animal rescue islands built from natural materials near their schools, documented in photographs, with interactive stations and workshop materials. Three classes were to be awarded for the most rescue islands for hedgehog, wolf and lynx; the proceeds from the sale of the photographs were intended for the Climate Fund Klagenfurt. Part of the EU project Climate Art City, the exhibition was organised by the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt with the kärnten.museum, the University of Klagenfurt and the Climate Fund Klagenfurt. Scientific supervision: Franz Rauch, Cornelia Malojer, Petra Korenjak and Stefanie Margarita Preiml (University of Klagenfurt); project lead: Katharina Kavallar (kärnten.museum). PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here. Source: stadtgalerie.net

Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. Under the title “Aus der Asche empor” (rising from the ashes), Sylvia Ofner shows sculpture and embroidery in the Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. From old oriental carpets, heirlooms and needlework of the 1930s she sews mythological figures: phoenix and centaur, Europa and the bull, Gilgamesh, Lamassu and the sphinx. With needle and thread she spins a story from the roots of Europe in Egypt and Mesopotamia to the present, a Europe that has reinvented itself again and again after wars and crises. The setting echoes the theme: the palace was built in the Renaissance, the age that saw itself as the rebirth of antiquity. Source: invitation of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia

Under the title “Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos” (epic paintings – between myth and cosmos), Ingrid Pröller shows large-format paintings, some up to five metres wide, in the vaulted Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. The cycle runs from archaic landscapes to futuristic images and asks how people, nature and the cosmos relate. In “Wildes Kind” and “Kretische Landschaft” consumer waste intrudes on idyllic landscapes; “Geburt” and “Fabel” take up motifs of creation and storytelling. The poster image “Endzeit” (2022) reads a coastal scene with a child, an octopus and dead animals as a passage to a new beginning, and “Matrix” shows a cosmonaut as a modern Odysseus. Pröller, born in Schärding in 1970 and trained at the Akademie der bildenden Künste in Vienna, paints many of her works in an open-air studio on Crete. Source: invitation and poster of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia; spittal-drau.at

The photographers Sebastian Köpcke and Volker Weinhold portray the artist Lisa Huber, born in Villach, in a photographic essay. They met as exhibiting artists at Admont Abbey and then photographed in her Berlin studio and in her workshop in the Haus der künstlerischen Begegnung in Villach. Their staged still lifes show objects from her life and work. The gallery hangs them next to large colour woodcuts by Lisa Huber. The exhibition is part of the Triennale IV Kärnten 2026. Source: villach.at, langenacht.orf.at

Nicoline von Heyl lives and works in Krumpendorf am Wörthersee. Her work moves between portrait and figure studies and non-representational, process-based painting. During the exhibition, the artist works on site in an open studio.

As Carinthia’s 2026 grant holder for photography and media art, Katharina Gruzei spent five months as artist in residence in the Europahaus studio provided by the City of Klagenfurt. The works, made between May and September, answer a summer marked by extreme heat and water scarcity: an analytical and humorous look at urban water spaces that places bodies and cityscape in an unusual state of suspension, between movement and stillness, everyday life and exception. Born in Klagenfurt in 1983, Gruzei works across photography, video, film, sound and installation, with a focus on socio-cultural themes and site-specific projects in public space.

A group exhibition curated by Ulli Sturm with thirty-five artists, among them Uwe Bressnik, whose World Record IV (2020) is the key image. Painting, graphic art and objects make the relationship between people and nature tangible across past, present and future: what a natural habitat once was, how humans changed the environment, and where hope lies. Twenty per cent of the proceeds from sales go to the Klagenfurt climate fund. All participants are recorded on this page.

Eighty years after the end of the Second World War, the Museum der Stadt Villach shows how wars end, in German and English. Six conflicts, from the Napoleonic Wars to the war in Ukraine, are linked to the history of Villach. Eleven eyewitnesses tell of flight, violence and new beginnings. Among the objects are a defused aerial bomb from the Second World War, a replica of an alpine position from the First World War and a Lada from Ukraine that was shot at by both sides. For 2026 the exhibition was extended and updated, with new content on the Cold War, the war in Ukraine and the sinking of the warship “Szent István”. It ends in a Peace Lab with interactive stations; two of them were developed by pupils of the BG/BRG Villach St. Martin. Source: villach.at, kaernten.orf.at, welcome2villach.at, klick-kaernten.at, it-gymnasium.at

Announcement. The Carinthian branch of the Berufsvereinigung bildender Künstler Österreichs invites to its BV flea market at the gallery, Feldkirchner Straße 31: painting, graphic art, small furniture and tableware from the members. The market opens on Monday, 28 September 2026 from 16:00 to 20:00 and runs from 29 September to 2 October 2026 during the gallery's opening hours. This is a sale, not an exhibition, so PERMAPHEMERA will not record it as a 360° tour. Source: bv-kaernten.at, "Aktuell" (flyer of September 2026).

The Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt devotes its winter exhibition “Alles Farbe” to Franz Grabmayr (1927–2015), the Carinthian-born painter whose thickly layered landscapes, sand pits and dance pictures made him one of Austria’s most distinctive post-war painters. Opening on 19 November 2026 at 18:00; further details have not been published yet. Source: stadtgalerie.net

Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. The Galerie Freihausgasse shows paintings by Gernot Fischer-Kondratovitch, born in Villach in 1968, under the title “vintage views from an unknown future”. According to the gallery they show pictures from a distant future: people, containers, houses and exotic animals in landscapes of ice and snow, or palm trees, beaches and seas in front of mountains. One of the works is from the series “Schneehaluzinationen” of 2026, acrylic on canvas, 100 × 140 cm. Source: villach.at

Under the title “Sehnsucht” (longing), the printmaker and songwriter Walther Preiml, who lives in Kötschach-Mauthen, shows new work at the stARTup gallery. His woodcuts and frottages revolve around a “painful longing for the unattainable”; according to the ORF programme, the mountains of the region, seen from Preiml’s own perspective, are at the centre. The exhibition opened during the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 October 2026, when the artist also performed songs of his own. It is on view until 31 December 2026, on Fridays from 17:00 to 19:00. Preiml had already exhibited prints at the gallery in 2024. Source: waltherpreiml.at, langenacht.orf.at

The Lebenshilfe Region Knittelfeld presents its art calendar “Hoffnung und Frieden” in a pop-up gallery in Knittelfeld, with the works for it on the walls. Artists of the Lebenshilfe with and without disabilities made it with Helmuth Ploschnitznigg and Adi Schmölzer, partly at a working morning with the Spielberg middle school on 24 March 2026. Works from the project also hung in the exhibition “Hoffnung & Frieden” at the Stadtgalerie Judenburg in April 2026. At the vernissage Johann Hubmann, chair of the Lebenshilfe, welcomed the guests, and the two artists spoke about how the calendar came about. Source: meinbezirk.at, kleinezeitung.at, lebenshilfe-knittelfeld.at, murtalinfo.at

Wolfgang Daborer, who lives in Spittal an der Drau, shows works from his cycle “Atemzüge” of 2025 and 2026 in the Wallnerhaus: mixed media on paper, 49.5 × 34.5 cm, and on linen, 200 × 35 cm. According to the flyer, the title refers to the line as a trace of breath. The lines come together, separate and open up space, with some accents of colour. The linen strips hang freely in the room. The exhibition opened on 21 May 2026 in the presence of Mayor Manfred Fleißner. Source: kleblach-lind.at, radio-osttirol.at

For his photo book Hometown, Arnold Pöschl portrayed one hundred people of the Carinthian capital: the director of the Stadttheater, Aron Stiehl, the stage director Ute Liepold, and figures from the graffiti, street-art and literary scenes. Together they draw a picture of a city between generations, cultures and social change, and a photographic counter-narrative to the cliché of a backward Klagenfurt. The exhibition opens at the Robert Musil Literatur-Museum on 16 September 2026 at 19:30 with the presentation of the book, and runs until the end of January 2027.

Armin Guerino’s practice bridges painting and art in public space. Landscape is his central theme, fed by travel and by his experiences in Africa. Recent works look at ecological change and extreme weather through motifs such as horizons, clouds, rain, cities and heads: the line becomes a trace, a path and a labyrinth; the city becomes landscape. Curated by Gabriele Ruff. The exhibition in the Alpen-Adria-Galerie at Theaterplatz 3 is free of charge. Source: stadtgalerie.net

The Living Studio of the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt announces an exhibition of works by Karlheinz Simonitsch. Opening on 1 December 2026 at 18:00; on view until 31 January 2027. Title and further details have not been published yet; the gallery reserves the right to make changes. Source: stadtgalerie.net

For the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 October 2026, the Galerie Palais Fugger in Klagenfurt showed oil paintings by the Carinthian painter Harald Scheicher under the title “Mediterraneo”. A grandson of Werner Berg, Scheicher has painted outdoors in front of the motif for decades; besides the landscape of southern Carinthia, painting journeys regularly take him to Istria, Dalmatia and Sicily. From 18:00 the artist guided visitors through the exhibition and was available for conversation; children could join tours, puzzle rallies and drawing. Whether the exhibition stayed on view after that night is not documented. Source: langenacht.orf.at, scheicher.cc

Santino Solace lives and works in Spittal an der Drau as a comic artist, illustrator and founder of the creative platform SolaceWorks. His work combines manga, comics and modern digital illustration in a personal, humorous narrative style. The exhibition offers insight into his projects, working processes and the development of his own worlds.

The association kultur.im.puls shows works by three graduates of the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste Kärnten in Klagenfurt: Inés Urach, Nicoline von Heyl and Roswitha Bucher-Sakowski. According to the organiser, the title “Blinddate der Perspektiven” (blind date of perspectives) refers to three separately developed positions meeting in one exhibition. Urach combines paper and paint in abstract pictures, von Heyl paints process-based works in mixed media, and Bucher-Sakowski paints figurative pictures in acrylic. The works hang in the daylit stairwell gallery of the Impuls Center; further works are on view in the stairwell of the Seeboden municipal office. Source: kultur-impuls.com, kaerntenportal.at, inesurach.at, nicolinevonheyl.com, bucher-sakowski.at

The international Alps-Adriatic joint exhibition of the Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur shows works by five artists from four municipalities in Friuli, Carinthia and Slovenia. Alda Grudina (Goriška Brda) shows flower paintings in oil, Alessandra Minin (Tavagnacco) abstract paintings and Ondina Altran (Monfalcone) paintings of the biblical story of Susanna and the Elders. Karl Nackler (Klagenfurt) shows white-on-black drawings of conductors, violinists and pianists as well as still lifes in colour; Marlis Lepicnik (Klagenfurt) shows women's faces. The exhibition continues the initiative's eleven-year exchange with the Gruppo artistico culturale Albrecht Dürer in Tavagnacco, the artists' association DABLO in Brda and the Circolo Culturale ENDAS in Monfalcone. Governor Daniel Fellner is the honorary patron; the Euregio Senza Confini, the Alps-Adriatic Alliance and the Alpe-Adria Center for Cross-border Cooperation (AACC) give their patronage. Source: invitation and poster of bewegungINkultur, meinbezirk.at, novice.at

For the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen 2026, the Kunstverein Velden showed the group exhibition “Spannungsfelder und Perspektiven” (fields of tension and perspectives) in the large and small halls on the first floor of the Europahaus in Klagenfurt. The works by members of the association circled around opposites, encounters and shifting points of view – the contrasts that arise where different things meet. The range of motifs, techniques and approaches was correspondingly wide, from gestural painting to drawing. The announcement named Siegfried Zellot, Gudrun Zikulnig, Slava Mohl, Alfred Scheikl and Sylvia Campidell. Guided tours started at 18:00, and the artists were present for conversation. The association from Velden am Wörther See has taken part in the Lange Nacht with themed exhibitions since 2004. PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here. Source: langenacht.orf.at, kunstverein-velden.at

Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. The association kultur.im.puls marks the tenth anniversary of the death of Klaus Zlattinger, who died in December 2016 and worked as an artist, art educator and gallerist. The exhibition presents a cross-section of his work together with works by artist friends, among them Wolfgang Daborer, Christine De Pauli, Otmar Eder and Karl Vouk; the complete list has not been published. At the vernissage Christine Strobl-Oman reads from the poetry volume “alles leben”, which includes photographic works by Zlattinger. Further works are on view in the Seeboden municipal office. Source: kultur-impuls.com

The Kunstverein postWERK devotes its annual exhibition at the Dinzlschloss to fragility, within the theme “schwach • šibko • debole” of the Triennale IV Kärnten 2026. Members and guest artists from Austria, Germany, Slovenia and Iran show painting, photography, installation, literature and performance. According to the organiser the exhibition treats tenderness as a state of attention, not of weakness. The works deal with vulnerability in material and in people, with fragile ecosystems and with a shared future. On the ORF Long Night of Museums on 3 October 2026, Christina Clar and Phil Yaeger performed “Wieso wir uns wiegen”. Source: villach.at, postwerk.at, langenacht.orf.at

On the ground floor of the Europahaus in Klagenfurt, Inés Urach showed the solo exhibition “Schwach.Unperfekt.Ausgefranst.Echt” (weak, imperfect, frayed, real) for the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen 2026. She announced it as a contribution to the Triennale IV Kärnten and its theme “schwach.šibko.debole”. The exhibition set cracks, breaks and frayed edges against the ideal of smooth, flawless surfaces and read them as traces of movement, time and resistance: imperfection not as a lack but as a form of honesty. Urach studied at the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Klagenfurt; she works abstractly and combines painting with paper and collaged elements. The artist was present for talks and guided tours from 18:00. PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here. Source: langenacht.orf.at, inesurach.at

Peter Kohlweiß has painted since 1982, beginning with Professor Hans Picottini at the HTL Villach and continuing through courses and seminars until he found his own style. He works in watercolour and drawing, translating what he sees on walks into pencil, brush and colour on paper and canvas.

Under the theme ‘Life stories – from tragedy to comedy’, visitors are invited to turn experiences, thoughts and texts into images. The festival combines an exhibition with daily workshops and a growing display of work created on site.

Hans Kupelwieser, born 1948 in Lunz am See, has spent four decades testing materials and space. Raumschatten brings anodised aluminium reliefs, photograms, magnifying-glass objects, rotating metal discs and stainless steel into six rooms of the Stadtgalerie: works that fuse sculpture and photography and unsettle how a room is perceived. Curated by Lisa Ortner-Kreil.

DIALOG is part of INSIEME, the tenth design experiment of ARS CARINTHIA – Kunst & Handwerk, with which the initiative also marks its 30th anniversary in 2026. At the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt two positions at a time answer each other in sequence: each pair starts from a freely chosen theme, first conceived for a defined space, real or imagined, and selected craft workshops realise the designs as active co-creators. The pairs are Esther Stocker and Matteo Thun, Sofia Podreka and Boris Podrecca, Laurids and Manfred Ortner, Karsten K. Krebs and HG Esch, Theres Cassini and Eva Schlegel, Sophie Grell and Ursula Klein, and Pepo Pichler and Walter Hösel; Tine Steinthaler works in exchange with an artificial intelligence. Curated by Walter Hösel. An exhibition of ARS CARINTHIA in cooperation with the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt. Source: stadtgalerie.net

Mit offenen Augen durchs Leben zu gehen und das Gesehene mit Stift, Pinsel und Farbe auf Papier und Leinwand zu gestalten, ist für ihn ein wunderbares Gefühl.

In der Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt antworten jeweils zwei Positionen nacheinander aufeinander: Jedes Paar geht von einem frei gewählten Thema aus, das zunächst für einen klar umrissenen realen oder imaginären Raum entworfen wird; ausgewählte Handwerksbetriebe setzen die Entwürfe als aktive Mitgestalter um. Die zwischen Mai und September entstandenen Arbeiten antworten auf einen Sommer, der von extremer Hitze und Wasserknappheit geprägt war: ein analytischer und humorvoller Blick auf städtische Wasserräume, der Körper und Stadtraum in einen ungewöhnlichen Schwebezustand versetzt – zwischen Bewegung und Stillstand, Alltag und Ausnahme. Gruzei, 1983 in Klagenfurt geboren, arbeitet mit Fotografie, Video, Film, Sound und Installation, mit Schwerpunkt auf soziokulturellen Themen und ortsspezifischen Projekten im öffentlichen Raum.

Jüngere Arbeiten betrachten ökologischen Wandel und Wetterextreme in Motiven wie Horizonten, Wolken, Regen, Städten und Köpfen: Die Linie wird zur Spur, zum Weg und zum Labyrinth; die Stadt wird zur Landschaft. Kuratiert von Gabriele Ruff. Die Ausstellung in der Alpen-Adria-Galerie am Theaterplatz 3 ist bei freiem Eintritt zugänglich. Quelle: stadtgalerie.net

Die Ausstellung wird am 16. September 2026 um 19:30 Uhr im Robert Musil Literatur-Museum eröffnet, zugleich wird der Bildband präsentiert. Sie läuft bis Ende Jänner 2027.

Der Kunstverein Velden zeigte zur ORF-Langen Nacht der Museen 2026 im großen und kleinen Saal im ersten Stock des Klagenfurter Europahauses die Gemeinschaftsausstellung „Spannungsfelder und Perspektiven“. Die Arbeiten von Vereinsmitgliedern kreisten um Gegensätze, Begegnungen und wechselnde Blickwinkel – um jene Kontraste, die entstehen, wo Unterschiedliches aufeinandertrifft. Entsprechend breit war das Spektrum an Motiven, Techniken und Zugängen, von gestischer Malerei bis zur Zeichnung. Angekündigt waren Siegfried Zellot, Gudrun Zikulnig, Slava Mohl, Alfred Scheikl und Sylvia Campidell. On the ground floor of the Europahaus in Klagenfurt, Inés Urach showed the solo exhibition “Schwach.Unperfekt.Ausgefranst.Echt” (weak, imperfect, frayed, real) for the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen 2026. She announced it as a contribution to the Triennale IV Kärnten and its theme “schwach.šibko.debole”. The exhibition set cracks, breaks and frayed edges against the ideal of smooth, flawless surfaces and read them as traces of movement, time and resistance: imperfection not as a lack but as a form of honesty. Urach studied at the Freie Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Klagenfurt; she works abstractly and combines painting with paper and collaged elements. The artist was present for talks and guided tours from 18:00. PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here. Source: langenacht.orf.at, inesurach.at

Im Erdgeschoß des Klagenfurter Europahauses zeigte Inés Urach zur ORF-Langen Nacht der Museen 2026 die Einzelausstellung „Schwach.Unperfekt.Ausgefranst.Echt“. Sie kündigte sie als Beitrag zur Triennale IV Kärnten mit dem Rahmenthema „schwach.šibko.debole“ an. Die Ausstellung stellte dem Ideal glatter, fehlerloser Oberflächen Risse, Brüche und ausgefranste Ränder gegenüber und las sie als Spuren von Bewegung, Zeit und Widerstand: das Unvollkommene nicht als Mangel, sondern als Ausdruck von Ehrlichkeit. Urach studierte an der Freien Akademie der Bildenden Künste in Klagenfurt; sie arbeitet abstrakt und verbindet Malerei mit Papier und collagierten Elementen. Ab 18 Uhr war die Künstlerin für Gespräche und Führungen anwesend. PERMAPHEMERA hat die Ausstellung als 360°-Tour aufgenommen; sie wird für die Veröffentlichung hier vorbereitet. Quelle: langenacht.orf.at, inesurach.at

Under the title “Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos” (epic paintings – between myth and cosmos), Ingrid Pröller shows large-format paintings, some up to five metres wide, in the vaulted Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. The cycle runs from archaic landscapes to futuristic images and asks how people, nature and the cosmos relate. In “Wildes Kind” and “Kretische Landschaft” consumer waste intrudes on idyllic landscapes; “Geburt” and “Fabel” take up motifs of creation and storytelling. The poster image “Endzeit” (2022) reads a coastal scene with a child, an octopus and dead animals as a passage to a new beginning, and “Matrix” shows a cosmonaut as a modern Odysseus. Pröller, born in Schärding in 1970 and trained at the Akademie der bildenden Künste in Vienna, paints many of her works in an open-air studio on Crete. Source: invitation and poster of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia; spittal-drau.at

Unter dem Titel „Epische Gemälde – Zwischen Mythos und Kosmos“ zeigt Ingrid Pröller großformatige Malerei, teils bis zu fünf Meter breit, im Gewölbe des Salamancakellers von Schloss Porcia. Der Zyklus reicht von archaischen Landschaften bis zu futuristischen Bildern und befragt das Verhältnis von Mensch, Natur und Kosmos. In „Wildes Kind“ und „Kretische Landschaft“ dringen Konsumreste in arkadische Naturräume ein; „Geburt“ und „Fabel“ greifen Motive von Schöpfung und Erzählung auf. Das Plakatmotiv „Endzeit“ (2022) deutet eine Küstenszene mit Kind, Oktopus und verendeten Tieren als Übergang zu einem Neubeginn, „Matrix“ zeigt einen Kosmonauten als modernen Odysseus. Pröller, 1970 in Schärding geboren und an der Akademie der bildenden Künste Wien ausgebildet, malt viele ihrer Bilder in einem Freiluftatelier auf Kreta. Quelle: Einladung und Plakat der Galerie im Schloss Porcia; spittal-drau.at

For the ORF Lange Nacht der Museen on 3 October 2026, the Galerie Palais Fugger in Klagenfurt showed oil paintings by the Carinthian painter Harald Scheicher under the title “Mediterraneo”. A grandson of Werner Berg, Scheicher has painted outdoors in front of the motif for decades; besides the landscape of southern Carinthia, painting journeys regularly take him to Istria, Dalmatia and Sicily. Announcement. This exhibition has not opened yet. Under the title “Aus der Asche empor” (rising from the ashes), Sylvia Ofner shows sculpture and embroidery in the Salamancakeller of Schloss Porcia. From old oriental carpets, heirlooms and needlework of the 1930s she sews mythological figures: phoenix and centaur, Europa and the bull, Gilgamesh, Lamassu and the sphinx. With needle and thread she spins a story from the roots of Europe in Egypt and Mesopotamia to the present, a Europe that has reinvented itself again and again after wars and crises. The setting echoes the theme: the palace was built in the Renaissance, the age that saw itself as the rebirth of antiquity. Source: invitation of the Galerie im Schloss Porcia

Ankündigung. Diese Ausstellung ist noch nicht eröffnet. Unter dem Titel „Aus der Asche empor“ zeigt Sylvia Ofner Skulptur und Stickerei im Salamancakeller von Schloss Porcia. Aus alten Orientteppichen, Erbstücken und Handarbeiten der 1930er-Jahre näht sie mythologische Gestalten: Phönix und Kentaur, Europa und den Stier, Gilgamesch, Lamassu und die Sphinx. Der Ort spiegelt das Thema: Das Schloss entstand in der Renaissance, der Epoche, die sich als Wiedergeburt der Antike verstand. Quelle: Einladung der Galerie im Schloss Porcia

Hans Kupelwieser, born 1948 in Lunz am See, has spent four decades testing materials and space. Raumschatten brings anodised aluminium reliefs, photograms, magnifying-glass objects, rotating metal discs and stainless steel into six rooms of the Stadtgalerie: works that fuse sculpture and photography and unsettle how a room is perceived. Curated by Lisa Ortner-Kreil.

Hans Kupelwieser, 1948 in Lunz am See geboren, erprobt seit vier Jahrzehnten Material und Raum. Kuratiert von Lisa Ortner-Kreil.

Part of the EU project Climate Art City, the exhibition was organised by the Stadtgalerie Klagenfurt with the kärnten.museum, the University of Klagenfurt and the Climate Fund Klagenfurt. Scientific supervision: Franz Rauch, Cornelia Malojer, Petra Korenjak and Stefanie Margarita Preiml (University of Klagenfurt); project lead: Katharina Kavallar (kärnten.museum). PERMAPHEMERA recorded the exhibition as a 360° tour, which is being prepared for publication here. Source: stadtgalerie.net

The international Alps-Adriatic joint exhibition of the Kulturinitiative bewegungINkultur shows works by five artists from four municipalities in Friuli, Carinthia and Slovenia. Karl Nackler (Klagenfurt) shows white-on-black drawings of conductors, violinists and pianists as well as still lifes in colour; Marlis Lepicnik (Klagenfurt) shows women's faces. The exhibition continues the initiative's eleven-year exchange with the Gruppo artistico culturale Albrecht Dürer in Tavagnacco, the artists' association DABLO in Brda and the Circolo Culturale ENDAS in Monfalcone. Governor Daniel Fellner is the honorary patron; the Euregio Senza Confini, the Alps-Adriatic Alliance and the Alpe-Adria Center for Cross-border Cooperation (AACC) give their patronage. Members and guest artists from Austria, Germany, Slovenia and Iran show painting, photography, installation, literature and performance. Eighty years after the end of the Second World War, the Museum der Stadt Villach shows how wars end, in German and English. Six conflicts, from the Napoleonic Wars to the war in Ukraine, are linked to the history of Villach. Eleven eyewitnesses tell of flight, violence and new beginnings. Among the objects are a defused aerial bomb from the Second World War, a replica of an alpine position from the First World War and a Lada from Ukraine that was shot at by both sides. A 360° photo is at first a flat image with an aspect ratio of 2:1. Only software turns it into a room in which the eye can move freely, and only many such images, properly linked, make a tour. For PERMAPHEMERA an application of its own has been in the making since 13 July 2026: the Tour Editor.

Its foundation is [Photo Sphere Viewer](https://photo-sphere-viewer.js.org/), an open-source library for 360° panoramas in the browser. The Tour Editor, a desktop application for the Mac, builds on it. It reads a folder of images and orders them by building, floor, room and standpoint. In the editor the standpoints are linked: markers on the floor lead from one standpoint to the next, notes explain individual works, and for every transition the direction of view on arrival can be set.

A feature that common virtual-tour software does not offer: every standpoint can be recorded from several heights, “High”, “Normal” and “Low”. A room can thus be seen at eye level, from above with an overview of how the works are arranged, or close to the floor, where sculptures and objects stand. For exhibitions whose effect depends on the room, this change of height is more than an effect.

So that details stay sharp when zooming in, the editor cuts every panorama into tiles, which the browser loads only where the view is directed. Finally it exports the finished tour; the website embeds it with the same viewer that runs in the editor. Neither part needs a server of its own.

Around 760 individual changes have gone into the software so far. It grows with every exhibition that is recorded: whatever one tour lacks is added for the next.

PERMAPHEMERA is not a word that comes easily on first hearing. It joins two terms that seem to contradict each other: “perma-” as in permanent, lasting, and “ephemera”, the fleeting.

Ephemera is a term from libraries and archives. It stands for printed matter made for a short time only: invitation cards, posters, programme leaflets, tickets. These are collected precisely because they show what happened on a particular day in a particular place. In this sense an exhibition is itself ephemera: carefully arranged, open for a few weeks, then taken down. PERMAPHEMERA keeps this fleeting thing permanently accessible. The name describes exactly the contradiction the project works on.

More reasons speak for it:

- **It is unmistakable.** As a newly formed word it cannot be confused with any common term, and a search for it leads to the archive rather than to a thousand other results.
- **It travels across languages.** Its Latin and Greek roots are familiar in German, English, Italian and Slovene alike, in a region where Carinthia, Friuli and Slovenia meet.
- **It describes instead of advertising.** The name promises nothing; it names a task.
- **It stays.** Once understood, it is kept: duration and transience in one word.

The lettering shows the idea. The H falls out of line and leans to one side, a sign that nothing stays quite as it was. And in the lower left corner of every page stands the small drawing “Fig. I. Temporary, yet enduring.”

Gezeichnete Zeichen, Fragmente von Architektur und gesättigte Farbflächen treffen in diesem Raum aufeinander, und genau dieses Zusammenspiel zeigt der 360°-Rundgang.

A 360° photo is at first a flat image with an aspect ratio of 2:1. Only software turns it into a room in which the eye can move freely, and only many such images, properly linked, make a tour. For PERMAPHEMERA an application of its own has been in the making since 13 July 2026: the Tour Editor.

Its foundation is [Photo Sphere Viewer](https://photo-sphere-viewer.js.org/), an open-source library for 360° panoramas in the browser. The Tour Editor, a desktop application for the Mac, builds on it. It reads a folder of images and orders them by building, floor, room and standpoint. In the editor the standpoints are linked: markers on the floor lead from one standpoint to the next, notes explain individual works, and for every transition the direction of view on arrival can be set.

A feature that common virtual-tour software does not offer: every standpoint can be recorded from several heights, “High”, “Normal” and “Low”. A room can thus be seen at eye level, from above with an overview of how the works are arranged, or close to the floor, where sculptures and objects stand. For exhibitions whose effect depends on the room, this change of height is more than an effect.

So that details stay sharp when zooming in, the editor cuts every panorama into tiles, which the browser loads only where the view is directed. Finally it exports the finished tour; the website embeds it with the same viewer that runs in the editor. Neither part needs a server of its own.

Around 760 individual changes have gone into the software so far. It grows with every exhibition that is recorded: whatever one tour lacks is added for the next.

Ein 360°-Foto ist zunächst ein flaches Bild im Seitenverhältnis 2:1. Erst eine Software macht daraus einen Raum, in dem sich der Blick frei bewegen kann, und erst viele solcher Bilder, richtig verbunden, ergeben einen Rundgang. Für PERMAPHEMERA entsteht dafür seit 13. Juli 2026 eine eigene Anwendung: der Tour Editor.

Die Grundlage ist [Photo Sphere Viewer](https://photo-sphere-viewer.js.org/), eine Open-Source-Bibliothek für 360°-Panoramen im Browser. Darauf baut der Tour Editor auf, eine Desktop-Anwendung für den Mac. Sie liest einen Ordner mit Aufnahmen und ordnet sie nach Gebäude, Geschoß, Raum und Standpunkt. Im Editor werden die Standpunkte verbunden: Markierungen am Boden führen von einem Standpunkt zum nächsten, Hinweise erklären einzelne Werke, und für jeden Übergang lässt sich festlegen, wohin der Blick beim Ankommen gerichtet ist.

Eine Besonderheit, die übliche Programme für virtuelle Rundgänge nicht bieten: Jeder Standpunkt kann aus mehreren Höhen aufgenommen werden, „High“, „Normal“ und „Low“. Ein Raum lässt sich so aus Augenhöhe betrachten, von oben mit dem Überblick über die Anordnung der Werke, oder nahe am Boden, wo Skulpturen und Objekte stehen. Für Ausstellungen, deren Wirkung vom Raum abhängt, ist dieser Wechsel der Höhe mehr als ein Effekt.

Damit Details auch beim Hineinzoomen scharf bleiben, zerlegt der Editor jedes Panorama in Kacheln, die der Browser nur dort lädt, wohin gerade geblickt wird. Am Ende exportiert er den fertigen Rundgang; die Website bindet ihn mit demselben Viewer ein, der auch im Editor läuft. Einen eigenen Server braucht keiner der beiden Teile.

Rund 760 einzelne Änderungen sind bis heute in die Software geflossen. Sie wächst mit jeder Ausstellung, die aufgenommen wird: Was bei einem Rundgang fehlt, wird für den nächsten ergänzt.

PERMAPHEMERA is not a word that comes easily on first hearing. It joins two terms that seem to contradict each other: “perma-” as in permanent, lasting, and “ephemera”, the fleeting.

Ephemera is a term from libraries and archives. It stands for printed matter made for a short time only: invitation cards, posters, programme leaflets, tickets. These are collected precisely because they show what happened on a particular day in a particular place. In this sense an exhibition is itself ephemera: carefully arranged, open for a few weeks, then taken down. PERMAPHEMERA keeps this fleeting thing permanently accessible. The name describes exactly the contradiction the project works on.

More reasons speak for it:

- **It is unmistakable.** As a newly formed word it cannot be confused with any common term, and a search for it leads to the archive rather than to a thousand other results.
- **It travels across languages.** Its Latin and Greek roots are familiar in German, English, Italian and Slovene alike, in a region where Carinthia, Friuli and Slovenia meet.
- **It describes instead of advertising.** The name promises nothing; it names a task.
- **It stays.** Once understood, it is kept: duration and transience in one word.

The lettering shows the idea. The H falls out of line and leans to one side, a sign that nothing stays quite as it was. And in the lower left corner of every page stands the small drawing “Fig. I. Temporary, yet enduring.”

PERMAPHEMERA ist kein Wort, das beim ersten Hören leicht von der Hand geht. Es verbindet zwei Begriffe, die einander zu widersprechen scheinen: „perma-“ wie permanent, dauerhaft, und „Ephemera“, das Flüchtige.

Ephemera ist ein Begriff aus Bibliotheken und Archiven. Er steht für Drucksachen, die nur für kurze Zeit gemacht sind: Einladungskarten, Plakate, Programmzettel, Eintrittskarten. Gerade sie werden gesammelt, weil sie zeigen, was an einem bestimmten Tag an einem bestimmten Ort geschah. Eine Ausstellung ist in diesem Sinn selbst Ephemera: sorgfältig eingerichtet, einige Wochen zugänglich, dann abgebaut. PERMAPHEMERA hält dieses Flüchtige dauerhaft zugänglich. Der Name beschreibt genau den Widerspruch, an dem das Projekt arbeitet.

Weitere Gründe sprechen für ihn:

- **Er ist unverwechselbar.** Als neu gebildetes Wort lässt er sich mit keinem gängigen Begriff verwechseln, und eine Suche danach führt zum Archiv statt zu tausend anderen Treffern.
- **Er versteht sich über Sprachgrenzen hinweg.** Die lateinischen und griechischen Wurzeln sind im Deutschen, Englischen, Italienischen und Slowenischen gleichermaßen geläufig, in einer Region, in der Kärnten, Friaul und Slowenien aneinandergrenzen.
- **Er beschreibt, statt zu werben.** Der Name verspricht nichts; er benennt eine Aufgabe.
- **Er bleibt.** Wer ihn einmal verstanden hat, behält ihn: Dauer und Vergänglichkeit in einem Wort.

Im Schriftzug ist der Gedanke sichtbar. Das H fällt aus der Reihe und neigt sich zur Seite, als Zeichen dafür, dass nichts ganz so bleibt, wie es war. Und in der linken unteren Ecke jeder Seite steht die kleine Zeichnung „Fig. I. Temporary, yet enduring.“: vergänglich und doch beständig.

A phoenix, a sphinx, figures from myths and legends: [Sylvia Ofner](/persons/sylvia-ofner/) shapes her figures from old oriental rugs and needlework. What once lay on the floor as a rug becomes a soft sculpture in her hands; embroideries accompany the figures. From 7 November the [Galerie im Schloss Porcia](/venues/galerie-im-schloss-porcia-spittal-drau/) in Spittal an der Drau shows these works under the title [“Aus der Asche empor – Skulptur und Stickerei”](/exhibitions/aus-der-asche-empor/).

- **Opening:** Friday, 6 November 2026, 7 pm
- **On view:** 7 November to 19 December 2026
- **Venue:** Galerie im Schloss Porcia, pillared vault of the Salamanca cellar, Spittal an der Drau

The exhibition is recorded for PERMAPHEMERA. From its last day, 19 December, it will be online as a 360° tour. Anyone who cannot make it to Spittal by then can see the figures as they were placed in the vault.

Ein Phönix, eine Sphinx, Gestalten aus Mythen und Legenden: [Sylvia Ofner](/persons/sylvia-ofner/) formt ihre Figuren aus alten Orientteppichen und Handarbeiten. Was einmal als Teppich am Boden lag, wird bei ihr zur weichen Skulptur; Stickereien begleiten die Figuren. Ab 7. November zeigt die [Galerie im Schloss Porcia](/venues/galerie-im-schloss-porcia-spittal-drau/) in Spittal an der Drau diese Arbeiten unter dem Titel [„Aus der Asche empor – Skulptur und Stickerei“](/exhibitions/aus-der-asche-empor/).

- **Vernissage:** Freitag, 6. November 2026, 19 Uhr
- **Laufzeit:** 7. November bis 19. Dezember 2026
- **Ort:** Galerie im Schloss Porcia, Säulengewölbe des Salamancakellers, Spittal an der Drau

Die Ausstellung wird für PERMAPHEMERA aufgenommen. Ab dem letzten Ausstellungstag, dem 19. Dezember, ist sie als 360°-Rundgang online. Wer es bis dahin nicht nach Spittal schafft, kann die Figuren dann so sehen, wie sie im Gewölbe aufgestellt waren.
